newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower in technical correction.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower in technical correction.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures pulled back sharply Wednesday, after recent sharp advances but dealers said the market's uptrend remained intact.

March delivery ended 2.90 cents per lb lower, at 144.55 cents, after ranging from 148.00 to 144.25. Second-month May finished down 3.35 cents, to 139.20 cents, while the outer months fell 3.25 to 3.65.

After rallying to fresh 18-month highs on Tuesday, traders said speculators took profits in a technical retracement. But sentiment remained strong despite profit-taking, as the market continued to be underpinned by supply concerns.

"The market was simply overdue for a correction," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes. "It is still constructive. There is the potential for smaller Brazilian and Colombian crops and a supply deficit."
"It might pull back a little more, but it should not change anything," she added.

Prices headed lower at the outset Wednesday, defying pre-opening expectations, as the market followed through on profit-taking seen yesterday. Traders said the March contract's failure Tuesday to rally much above the 150.00-cent level disappointed some operators, who were looking to test the 155.00-cent level.
On the charts, traders pegged support at 143.50-143.25 in the March contract, followed by 142.15. On the upside, 150.00 would still provide a key psychological hurdle, they said.
Volume Wednesday reached an estimated 10,385 lots, down from Tuesday's official tally of 16,578 lots.
